{"self_assessment": "Impact
I proposed the big fish concept in the first seconds: a nose start, one line over the back and one under the belly, and a forked tail. The outline is simple and recognizable to a judge who doesn't know the plan. The finished picture follows that design, and by our last check all 131 standing dominoes were connected to the start.

Execution
I laid the start domino and the first stretch of the top line from the nose, then moved out to the middle of the back and laid on from there so the top line could be built from two ends at once. I inspected the run several times, including after the middle of the back was laid, to check that the chain was connected. Once the fish was complete, I held my hands off the table. With bumps being the main remaining risk, that was the right call.

Collaboration
I split the work early so people weren't stacked on one line: the top line for me, the bottom line and the tail for others. I redirected Priya to carry the top line forward from its end while I moved to the middle of the back. I kept the table updated on what I was doing and what I'd seen in my checks. When Tom took the upper fork, I stayed off it so we didn't crowd each other.

Leadership
I set the direction quickly, which let the table start building within the first minute. I assigned lines and adjusted when the top line turned out to be the slow one. In the last stretch I kept the table calm and focused on a hands-off finish. I believe my share of the result was about a third, mainly the concept, the early layout, and coordinating the top line.", "my_share_percent": 33}
